children: North Macedonia's Energy Ministry held talks with a delegation of 20 Japanese companies and institutions on November 19, focusing on investment opportunities and long-term cooperation in the energy sector, the ministry said.

The meetings took place at the government building during a visit organised by the Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO), in cooperation with the Japanese Embassy in North Macedonia and under the patronage of Japanese Ambassador Setsuko Kawahara.

Representatives of the Ministry of Energy, Mining and Mineral Resources, state-owned power transmission operator MEPSO and electricity producer ESM presented the country's energy sector potential, ongoing and planned projects, and development priorities. The Japanese delegation was briefed on investment opportunities and discussed potential areas for future cooperation.

Among the Japanese companies and financial institutions showing particular interest were Hitachi Energy, Hitachi Europe, Marubeni Corporation, Sumitomo Heavy Industries, MUFG Bank and Nippon Export and Investment Insurance (NEXI).
The delegation included companies with experience in developing and modernising electricity infrastructure, industrial technologies and investment financing.

The visit aims to strengthen links between North Macedonia's energy institutions and companies and Japanese technological, investment and financial partners, potentially paving the way for new investments, infrastructure modernisation and progress in the country's energy transition.

title: North Macedonia discusses energy investment opportunities with Japanese companies
